faqs.question: What is shockwave therapy and how is it different from cold laser?
faqs.answer: Shockwave therapy uses acoustic pressure waves to stimulate tissue healing and break up scar tissue. Cold laser uses specific light wavelengths to reduce inflammation and accelerate cellular repair. Both are non-invasive and complement chiropractic care, especially for peripheral neuropathy.

faqs.question: Is chiropractic safe during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: Yes. Chiropractic care during pregnancy is widely used to address back and pelvic pain, support proper fetal positioning, and ease delivery. Stenzel Chiropractic uses techniques and tables designed for pregnancy.

faqs.question: What is bioidentical hormone replacement therapy?
faqs.answer: Bioidentical hormone replacement therapy uses hormones that are structurally identical to those your body produces naturally. Unlike synthetic hormones, BHRT is customized to your individual needs and often results in fewer side effects with better symptom relief.

faqs.question: Who is a good candidate for hormone replacement therapy?
faqs.answer: Women experiencing menopause or perimenopause symptoms, men with low testosterone, and anyone with diagnosed hormone deficiencies may benefit from hormone optimization. A comprehensive evaluation determines your candidacy.

faqs.question: Is hormone therapy covered by insurance?
faqs.answer: Many hormone therapy services may be considered preventive or wellness-focused and may not be covered by insurance. We work with patients to understand their coverage and provide transparent pricing for all services.

faqs.question: How is functional medicine different from conventional primary care?
faqs.answer: Functional medicine seeks to identify and address the root causes of disease rather than just treating symptoms. We take time to understand your unique health history, genetics, and lifestyle to create a personalized treatment plan.

faqs.question: What does the first appointment look like?
faqs.answer: Your first appointment includes a comprehensive health history, physical examination, and specialized lab testing. This allows us to assess your current hormone levels and overall health status before recommending a treatment plan.

faqs.question: How long until I feel a difference?
faqs.answer: Most patients notice improvements in energy, mood, and sleep within 2 to 4 weeks. Full optimization typically takes 3 to 6 months as we fine-tune your dosages based on how you feel and your lab work.

faqs.question: Do you work with men as well as women?
faqs.answer: Yes. We work with both men and women. Men often benefit from testosterone optimization, which can improve energy, mood, muscle mass, and overall vitality.

faqs.question: What are peptides and how do they help?
faqs.answer: Peptides are short chains of amino acids that can improve hormone production, accelerate healing, enhance muscle growth, and support metabolic function. They represent the future of regenerative and optimization medicine.

team_members.name: Dr. Jessica Pearson
team_members.bio: Dr. Jess combines her background in traditional medicine with her passion for holistic, whole-body care. Born and raised in South Dakota, she completed her medical degree at USD and her OB/GYN residency in Georgia before serving in the U.S. Air Force. There, she became Medical Director of Women's Health and later Associate Program Director of an OB/GYN residency program. Along the way, Dr. Jess discovered functional medicine and fell in love with its ability to uncover the why behind health struggles rather than just treat symptoms. Today, she specializes in women's health, hormone balance, and supporting strong, healthy pregnancies. With additional training in perinatal fitness, she empowers women at every stage of fertility, pregnancy, and motherhood. Outside the clinic, you will find her doing CrossFit, triathlons, or hiking with her rescue pup, Zora. Patients describe Dr. Jess as both knowledgeable and approachable, someone who listens deeply, explains clearly, and helps women feel truly cared for.

team_members.name: Dr. Cheryl Bones
team_members.bio: For Dr. Cheryl, chiropractic and functional medicine are personal. Growing up, she faced her own GI struggles and injuries that conventional care could not resolve. Everything changed when she worked with a chiropractor and functional medicine doctor who finally gave her hope and lasting relief. Inspired, she set out to do the same for others. Dr. Cheryl earned her Doctorate of Chiropractic at Northwestern Health Sciences University and is certified in functional medicine through the Institute for Functional Medicine. She works with patients of all ages, blending chiropractic care, muscle and fascial work, cranial therapy, and functional medicine to address concerns ranging from GI dysfunction and skin issues to sinus problems, POTS, and pediatric care. She grew up on a farm near Tripp, SD, and now lives near Parker with her husband Dan (a farmer and retired Air Force Guard member) and their three children. Patients appreciate Dr. Cheryl's ability to uncover root causes and create individualized plans that bring real, lasting improvements.

team_members.name: Sam Niewenhuis
team_members.bio: Sam brings both professional expertise and personal experience to his work in primary care and functional medicine. After earning his nursing degree and Family Nurse Practitioner degree from SDSU, he gained extensive experience in emergency medicine, internal medicine, and urgent care across Sioux Falls health systems. When his own family faced health challenges that conventional medicine could not solve, Sam sought alternative answers and discovered functional medicine — and it transformed not only his family's health but also his approach to patient care. At Prairie Roots, Sam helps men, women, and children get to the root of health concerns with a focus on practical, whole-person solutions. He is passionate about guiding patients out of the system and into care that is personalized, thoughtful, and truly patient-centered. Outside of work, Sam is a devoted husband and father to four children. He enjoys spending time outdoors, gardening, and tending to his backyard chickens. Patients value Sam's down-to-earth approach, relatability, and commitment to providing high-quality care outside the traditional system.

team_members.name: Dr. Sarah Tadlock
team_members.bio: Born and raised in Sioux Falls, Dr. Sarah has always been passionate about movement and performance — from her early days as a competitive soccer player and gymnast to her career as an athletic trainer. Eventually, her love for helping people heal and thrive led her to chiropractic care. After earning her doctorate at Northwestern Health Sciences University, Dr. Sarah worked in Minnesota before moving home to Sioux Falls. She has a special focus on moms and babies, bringing together her chiropractic expertise and training as a doula to support women through pregnancy, birth, and postpartum recovery. When she is not at Prairie Roots Health, Dr. Sarah is coaching at CrossFit KOTA, cheering people on as they grow stronger inside and out. Patients often describe Dr. Sarah as compassionate, encouraging, and uniquely skilled at supporting both mamas and their little ones as well as athletes.

about: Midwest Hyperbarics is Sioux Falls' first dedicated HBOT specialty clinic. Under the guidance of Jada Hieb, NP, the clinic brings hard-shell hyperbaric oxygen therapy protocols to the region for recovery, chronic conditions, and performance optimization.

HBOT is one of the most exciting frontiers in regenerative medicine, with applications ranging from wound healing and concussion recovery to anti-aging and athletic performance optimization. Hard-shell hyperbaric chambers deliver treatments at 1.5-3.0 ATA (atmospheres absolute), providing significantly greater oxygen delivery than soft-shell or mild chambers, with protocols tailored to each patient's condition.

Oxygen is the body's primary healing agent. By dramatically increasing tissue oxygen levels, HBOT activates over 8,000 genes involved in healing, growth, and repair, making it one of the most powerful regenerative therapies available. Emerging research shows HBOT benefits for neurological conditions, autoimmune disorders, Lyme disease, chronic fatigue syndrome, and age-related cognitive decline. Athletes use HBOT to accelerate recovery between training sessions.

New patients at Midwest Hyperbarics will find a professional, patient-centered environment designed to put you at ease from the moment you walk in. The team takes time to listen to your concerns, answer your questions, and explain recommended approaches to care.

faqs.question: What is hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT)?
faqs.answer: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy involves breathing pure oxygen inside a pressurized chamber. The increased pressure allows your lungs to take in significantly more oxygen, which supports healing, reduces inflammation, and drives cellular repair.

faqs.question: What's the difference between hard-shell and soft-shell HBOT chambers?
faqs.answer: Hard-shell chambers operate at higher pressures (up to 2.0 ATA or more) and deliver medical-grade protocols. Soft-shell chambers operate at lower pressures (typically 1.3 ATA). Midwest Hyperbarics is a dedicated hard-shell specialty clinic.

faqs.question: What conditions can HBOT help with?
faqs.answer: HBOT supports recovery from post-surgical healing, traumatic brain injury, stroke recovery, chronic wounds, inflammatory conditions, persistent fatigue, athletic recovery, and general performance optimization.

faqs.question: How long is a typical HBOT session?
faqs.answer: A single session runs 60 to 90 minutes, plus pressurization and depressurization time. Most protocols involve 10 to 40 sessions over several weeks.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover HBOT?
faqs.answer: Coverage varies by condition and carrier. Some FDA-approved indications may be covered, but most wellness and optimization protocols are self-pay. Contact the clinic for details.

faqs.question: Do I need a referral to start HBOT?
faqs.answer: No referral is required. New clients begin with a suitability evaluation to determine whether HBOT is a good fit.

Founded by Gabrielle Hoing, who spent more than two decades in geriatric care and helped build 11 private duty agencies across 8 states, Kore Cares brings deep expertise and compassionate service to families navigating one of life's biggest transitions.

What started as a mission to bring professional, trustworthy in-home care to South Dakota has grown into a statewide agency serving 43 counties and 111 cities. Whether your parent needs help after surgery, your family member is managing dementia, you're supporting a veteran, or you're not sure yet what level of care is needed, Kore Cares meets families where they are.

The team is built on three promises: trained, vetted caregivers who show up; transparent communication so families always know what's happening; and the flexibility to adjust care as life changes. Carly King, Agency Manager, and her team handle everything from initial assessment through ongoing coordination, so your family can focus on what matters.

faqs.question: What are the signs someone needs in-home care?
faqs.answer: Common early behaviors include exhaustion after light housework, avoiding the shower for fear of falling, skipping physician visits to avoid a care recommendation, unexplained weight loss, and driving changes. Many families wait until a crisis, such as a fall, stroke, or hospital stay, forces the call.

faqs.question: What is the difference between home care and home health care?
faqs.answer: Home health care is typically Medicare-covered, tied to a physician order, and focused on skilled therapy after an illness or hospital stay. Home care is non-medical daily support: bathing, dressing, meal prep, laundry, medication setups, companionship, and ongoing nursing services. Kore Cares offers both.

faqs.question: Does Medicare cover in-home care?
faqs.answer: Medicare covers short-term skilled services such as physical, occupational, and speech therapy after a qualifying hospital stay. Medicare does not cover custodial or personal care at home. For non-medical home care, payer options are Medicaid, the VA, long-term care insurance, or private pay.

faqs.question: How do Medicaid, the VA, and long-term care insurance pay for home care?
faqs.answer: Medicaid covers qualifying non-medical home care for eligible South Dakota residents. The VA has multiple programs covering home care for veterans. Long-term care insurance policies pay out based on the individual policy terms. Kore Cares helps families navigate all three.

faqs.question: How do I choose a trustworthy home care agency?
faqs.answer: Ask about mission and ownership, caregiver training process, CPR and dementia certifications, background-check practices, quality assurance systems, and how the agency handles backup coverage when a caregiver calls out. South Dakota does not currently regulate private-pay home care, which makes these questions essential.

faqs.question: What are red flags when hiring a home care agency?
faqs.answer: Watch for vague answers about training, no dementia certification, no documented quality assurance process, no plan for caregiver no-shows, unclear ownership, or inability to produce background-check records for the specific caregiver being assigned.

faqs.question: How do I talk to my parent about getting a caregiver?
faqs.answer: Start with observations rather than conclusions. Frame the ask around yourself if needed. Give them time. Most people come around when they think about the impact their health has on the people around them.

faqs.question: Is in-home care only for seniors?
faqs.answer: No. Kore Cares serves anyone 18 and older, plus pediatric cases on a case-by-case basis. Clients include people recovering from surgery or injury, people living with disabilities, and people managing chronic illness.

faqs.question: What is a care plan in home care?
faqs.answer: A written plan that defines what the caregiver will help with each visit, customized to the client's physical needs, cognitive status, home environment, and family preferences. Care plans are updated as needs change.

faqs.question: What is Care Connection?
faqs.answer: Kore Cares' intake service for families who know they need help but are not sure what kind. A care coordinator meets with the family, assesses the situation, and maps the options.
